question_text: What is the standard and correct document sequence followed in an accounting system when purchasing raw materials from a vendor?
option_a: Purchase Order (PO) -> Goods Receipt Note (GRN) -> Vendor Purchase Invoice -> Payment
option_b: Vendor Invoice -> Purchase Order -> Goods Receipt Note
option_c: Payment -> Purchase Order -> Goods Receipt Note
option_d: Goods Receipt Note -> Purchase Order -> Payment
explanation: Standard P2P workflow begins with an approved Purchase Order, followed by Goods Receipt Note on arrival, Vendor Invoice entry, and Payment.

question_text: Before approving a vendor's invoice for payment, what does the 3-Way Match verify?
option_a: Approved Purchase Order terms/prices, Physical Goods Receipt Note (GRN) quantities, and Vendor Invoice billed amounts
option_b: Customer Sales Order, Credit Limit, and Dispatch Slip
option_c: Bank Balance, Cheque Counterfoil, and Cash Book
option_d: Employee Attendance, Leave Log, and Salary Slip
explanation: 3-Way match ensures the company only pays for authorized goods actually received at agreed PO rates.

question_text: When receiving liquid inks or adhesives at the factory gate, which parameters must the accountant verify on the weighbridge slip before posting the GRN?
option_a: Gross weight of the vehicle/drums, tare weight of empty containers, net weight in KGs/Liters, and batch number
option_b: Customer sales order number only
explanation: Liquid raw materials require verification of gross weight, tare weight, net quantity in KGs/Liters, and batch numbers.

question_text: When raw material paper reels are received into the factory warehouse against a PO before the vendor invoice arrives, what is the accounting entry?
option_a: Debit Raw Material Inventory Account | Credit Unbilled Goods Received Clearing Account
option_b: Debit Vendor Account | Credit Bank Account
option_c: Debit Cost of Goods Sold | Credit Vendor Account
option_d: Debit Sales Account | Credit Inventory Account
explanation: Receiving inventory increases asset stock (Debit Inventory) and creates a temporary liability for unbilled goods (Credit Unbilled Goods Clearing).

question_text: When an advance payment of Rs 1,00,000 is paid to a supplier before dispatch of paper reels, what is the journal entry in the accounts?
option_a: Debit Advance to Suppliers Account (Current Asset) Rs 1,00,000 | Credit Bank Account Rs 1,00,000
option_b: Debit Purchase Expense Account | Credit Cash Account
option_c: Debit Sales Account | Credit Vendor Account
option_d: Debit Profit & Loss Account | Credit Bank Account
explanation: Supplier advances are classified as Current Assets until the final purchase invoice is booked.

question_text: If 10 out of 100 drums of adhesive are rejected due to substandard quality, which document is issued to the vendor to reduce our payable balance?
option_a: Debit Note (Purchase Return Note)
option_b: Credit Note
explanation: A buyer issues a Debit Note to reduce the accounts payable balance for returned or rejected goods.

question_text: When creating a new vendor ledger in accounting software, which mandatory tax details are required to claim valid GST Input Tax Credit (ITC)?
option_a: Valid 15-digit GSTIN, Permanent Account Number (PAN), and registered state code
option_b: Vendor's website URL only
option_c: Number of machines in vendor's factory
explanation: Valid GSTIN and PAN are mandatory for tax compliance, e-Way bills, and GSTR-2B credit matching.

question_text: How should transportation freight charges incurred to bring raw material paper reels from the rail yard to the factory be recorded?
option_a: Debited to Freight Inward Account (Direct Cost added to cost of inventory/purchases)
option_b: Debited to Freight Outward Account (Selling Expense)
explanation: Freight Inward is a direct cost incurred to bring inventory to its present location, forming part of purchase cost.

question_text: If paper reels are purchased in Kilograms (KGs) but used in Square Meters (Sq. Mtr), what calculation must the accountant perform?
option_a: Apply the paper GSM (Grams per Sq. Meter) formula: Area (Sq. Mtr) = Weight (Grams) / GSM
option_b: Multiply KGs by total customer sales orders
option_c: Divide invoice price by employee count
explanation: In paper operations, converting weight (KGs) to surface area (Sq. Meters) relies on Grammage (GSM).

question_text: What is the purpose of generating an Accounts Payable (A/P) Aging Report at the end of each week?
option_a: To categorize unpaid vendor bills by due date intervals (e.g. 0-30 days, 31-60 days) to schedule payments and monitor overdue liabilities
option_b: To calculate employee annual income tax
explanation: A/P Aging reports categorize outstanding vendor balances by age intervals to plan cash outflows.

question_text: What internal control rule prevents an accountant from accidentally entering and paying the exact same vendor bill twice?
option_a: Validating the Vendor's Original Invoice Number and Date in the system before saving the voucher
option_b: Deleting all vendor ledgers at the end of each month
option_c: Paying all vendors strictly in physical cash
explanation: Checking the unique Vendor Invoice Reference Number prevents duplicate booking and double payment.

question_text: Under Section 43B(h) of the Income Tax Act, what happens if an overdue payment to a registered Micro or Small enterprise is not made within the agreed timeline (max 45 days)?
option_a: The deduction for the expense is disallowed in the current financial year and added back to taxable profit
option_b: The payment is permanently waived by the government
option_c: The company's bank account is automatically frozen
explanation: Under Section 43B(h), any sum payable to an MSME enterprise beyond 45 days (or 15 days without agreement) is disallowed as a tax deduction in that year.

question_text: What is the standard document sequence for a customer order from quotation to payment collection?
option_a: Sales Quotation -> Sales Order (SO) -> Delivery Challan -> Tax Invoice -> Payment Receipt
option_b: Tax Invoice -> Purchase Order -> Goods Receipt Note
option_c: Payment Receipt -> Delivery Note -> Purchase Request
option_d: Delivery Note -> Sales Quotation -> Outgoing Payment
explanation: Standard O2C document flow begins with Sales Quotation, confirmed Sales Order, Goods Dispatch/Delivery Challan, Tax Invoice, and Payment Receipt.

question_text: When finished goods are dispatched and invoiced to a customer for Rs 2,00,000 + 12% GST, what is the accounting entry?
option_a: Debit Customer Debtors Account Rs 2,24,000 | Credit Sales Revenue Account Rs 2,00,000, Credit Output GST Liability Rs 24,000
option_b: Debit Cash Account | Credit Purchase Account
option_c: Debit Sales Account | Credit Bank Account
option_d: Debit Inventory Account | Credit Customer Account
explanation: Invoicing a credit customer debits trade receivables (Gross Rs 2,24,000), credits sales revenue (Net Rs 2,00,000), and credits output tax liability (Rs 24,00,0).

question_text: If a client rejects 500 damaged items after receiving the invoice, which document does our company issue to reduce their balance?
option_a: Credit Note (Sales Return Note)
option_b: Debit Note
explanation: A seller issues a Credit Note to credit the customer's ledger, reducing accounts receivable and reversing output tax liability.

question_text: Under Indian GST rules, what is the mandatory consignment value threshold above which an E-Way Bill is required for inter-state transport of goods?
explanation: Under GST rules, an E-Way bill is mandatory for movement of goods of consignment value exceeding Rs 50,000.

question_text: When a customer deposits a 50% advance of Rs 50,000 before manufacturing begins, what is the initial accounting entry?
option_a: Debit Bank Account Rs 50,000 | Credit Customer Advance Liability Account Rs 50,000
option_b: Debit Sales Account | Credit Bank Account
option_c: Debit Customer Account | Credit Capital Account
option_d: Debit Inventory Account | Credit Cash Account
explanation: Customer advances received are recorded as a Current Liability until final goods are dispatched and billed.

question_text: Under Indian GST, which HSN chapter covers cartons, boxes, and cases made of paper or paperboard?
option_a: Chapter 48 (HSN 4819)
option_b: Chapter 84 (Industrial Machinery)
explanation: Cartons, boxes, cases, bags and other packing containers of paper/paperboard are classified under HSN 4819 (Chapter 48).

question_text: If a customer has an authorized credit limit of Rs 5,00,000 and currently owes Rs 4,80,000, what should the accounts team do if a new dispatch order of Rs 60,000 is requested?
option_a: Hold the dispatch and request an on-account payment or seek formal managerial approval for a credit limit override
option_b: Dispatch the goods immediately without informing management
option_c: Delete the customer's previous ledger balance
option_d: Increase the invoice price by 50% without asking
explanation: Credit control policies require holding dispatches that breach credit limits until overdue payments are cleared or formal approval is granted.

question_text: When a customer settles an outstanding invoice of Rs 1,18,000 via NEFT bank transfer, what is the accounting entry?
option_a: Debit Bank Account Rs 1,18,000 | Credit Customer Debtors Account Rs 1,18,000
option_b: Debit Customer Account | Credit Sales Revenue
option_c: Debit Sales Revenue | Credit Bank Account
option_d: Debit Inventory Account | Credit Cash Account
explanation: Recording customer payment receipt: Debit Bank Account (asset increase), Credit Customer Debtors (receivable decrease).

question_text: Why must a physical printed Delivery Challan accompany every factory dispatch truck during transit?
option_a: To provide legal transit documentation for factory gate security, highway checks, and customer receiving acknowledgement
option_b: To act as the company's annual financial report
option_c: It is only required if the truck breaks down
option_d: To replace the driver's driving license
explanation: Delivery Challans document the physical custody, quantity, and description of goods during transport and provide proof of receipt.

question_text: When factory waste paper trim scrap is sold to a scrap merchant for Rs 1,00,000 + GST, what TCS rate must be collected under Section 206C(1)?
option_a: 1% TCS on total invoice value
option_b: 10% TDS
explanation: Section 206C(1) of the Income Tax Act mandates collecting 1% TCS on the commercial sale of scrap generated from manufacturing.

question_text: Which management report allows the accounts team to track customer balances overdue beyond 30, 60, 90, and 180 days?
option_a: Accounts Receivable (A/R) Aging Report
option_b: Bank Statement
explanation: The A/R Aging Report tracks open customer invoices by time past due to follow up on collections and manage credit risk.

question_text: Why does the accounts department send periodic Balance Confirmation Statements to customers at year-end?
option_a: To verify ledger balances, detect unrecorded credit notes or disputed invoices, and obtain written audit evidence
option_b: To cancel all outstanding customer debts
option_c: To calculate the factory electricity bill
explanation: Balance confirmations reconcile customer accounts, identify disputed billings or unrecorded credits, and provide audit support.

topic: Issue of Material to Factory Shop Floor
question_text: When raw materials are issued from the main warehouse to the factory production shop floor, what is the accounting entry?
option_a: Debit Production Material Consumption Account | Credit Raw Material Inventory Account
option_b: Debit Customer Account | Credit Sales Account
option_c: Debit Profit & Loss Account | Credit Bank Account
option_d: Debit Share Capital | Credit Cash Account
explanation: Issuing material to the shop floor transfers value from Raw Material inventory to manufacturing consumption.

question_text: When finished manufactured goods are packed and moved into the finished goods warehouse, what is the accounting entry?
option_a: Debit Finished Goods Inventory Account | Credit Manufacturing Production Account
option_b: Debit Purchase Expense | Credit Vendor Account
option_c: Debit Sales Account | Credit Finished Goods Inventory
option_d: Debit Bank Account | Credit Capital Account
explanation: Booking completed production transfers costs from manufacturing operations into Finished Goods inventory asset.

question_text: When paper cutting scrap is generated on the factory floor, how should this scrap be accounted for in the books?
option_a: Record scrap stock quantity in inventory and credit manufacturing production cost
option_b: Ignore the scrap completely
option_c: Debit the customer's personal bank account
option_d: Increase the invoice price of previous year sales
explanation: Production scrap must be recorded as scrap inventory, and its estimated value reduces net manufacturing cost.

question_text: If physical stock count reveals that physical ink stock is 450 KGs but the book stock shows 480 KGs (30 KGs shortage), what is the correct adjustment?
option_a: Debit Stock Shortage / Loss Account Rs (Value of 30 KGs) | Credit Raw Material Inventory Account
option_b: Increase customer sales invoices by 30 KGs
explanation: Physical inventory shortages must be written off to a Stock Loss account to align book stock with reality.

question_text: Which standard inventory valuation method assumes that the oldest raw material batches purchased are the first ones issued to production?
option_a: FIFO (First In, First Out)
option_b: LIFO (Last In, First Out)
explanation: FIFO assumes that inventory purchased first is consumed first, valuing ending stock at the most recent purchase prices.

question_text: How should machine lubrication grease, strapping rolls, and plant cleaning solvents be classified in the financial accounts?
option_a: Factory Consumables & Stores Expense (Indirect Manufacturing Overheads)
option_b: Director Salary
explanation: Consumables like grease, tape, and strapping are operational stores categorized as indirect factory overheads.

question_text: If 1,000 KGs of material are in stock @ Rs 50/KG and a new batch of 2,000 KGs is purchased @ Rs 56/KG, what is the new Weighted Average Cost per KG?
option_b: Rs 50.00 per KG
explanation: Weighted Average Cost = Total Value (50,000 + 1,12,000 = 1,62,000) / Total Quantity (3,000) = Rs 54.00/KG.

question_text: When raw materials are destroyed in a godown water-leakage incident, what is the mandatory GST requirement under Section 17(5)(h)?
option_a: Write off inventory to P&L and reverse the corresponding Input Tax Credit previously availed in GSTR-3B
option_b: Claim double GST refund from government
option_c: Sell the damaged stock as prime quality
explanation: Section 17(5)(h) mandates that Input Tax Credit availed on goods lost, stolen, destroyed, or written off must be reversed.

question_text: In a manufacturing facility, how is the wages of machine operators classified compared to factory security guards?
option_a: Machine operators are Direct Labor (Cost of Production); Security guards are Indirect Labor (Factory Overheads)
option_b: Both are Selling Expenses
explanation: Wages of workers directly engaged in fabrication are Direct Labor; plant support staff wages are Indirect Labor overheads.

question_text: What is the primary audit objective of conducting a physical stock-taking count on March 31st?
option_a: To physically verify existence, condition, and valuation of inventories reported on the Balance Sheet
option_b: To calculate employee bonus
explanation: Year-end physical inventory verification confirms existence, completeness, condition, and balance sheet valuation.

question_text: What is the primary objective of preparing a monthly Bank Reconciliation Statement (BRS)?
option_a: To explain and reconcile timing and clerical differences between the internal Cash Book bank ledger and the Bank Statement balance
option_b: To calculate employee annual income tax
option_d: To determine selling prices of goods
explanation: BRS reconciles internal bank ledgers with the bank statement, identifying unpresented cheques, direct deposits, and charges.

question_text: When a vendor payment cheque of Rs 2,00,000 issued on March 29 is presented to the bank on April 4, how is it handled in the March 31 BRS starting from Cash Book balance?
option_a: Added back to Cash Book balance to reconcile to Bank Statement balance
option_b: Deducted from Cash Book balance
explanation: Cheques issued were already deducted in Cash Book; to reconcile to the higher bank statement balance, they are added back.

question_text: When the bank debits Rs 590 (Rs 500 charges + Rs 90 GST) as monthly account charges, what is the journal entry in the accounts?
option_a: Debit Bank Charges Account Rs 500, Debit Input GST Account Rs 90 | Credit Bank Account Rs 590
option_b: Debit Customer Account Rs 590 | Credit Bank Account Rs 590
option_c: Debit Sales Account Rs 590 | Credit Cash Account Rs 590
option_d: Debit Inventory Account Rs 590 | Credit Vendor Account Rs 590
explanation: Bank charges are an operating expense with claimable Input GST: Debit Bank Charges, Debit Input GST, Credit Bank.

question_text: When a customer's payment cheque of Rs 50,000 bounces due to insufficient funds, what entry must the accountant make?
option_a: Debit Customer Debtors Account Rs 50,000 | Credit Bank Account Rs 50,000
option_b: Debit Sales Revenue | Credit Purchase Account
option_c: Debit Profit & Loss Account | Credit Capital Account
explanation: A dishonoured cheque reverses the original receipt: Debit Customer Debtors (re-establishing receivable), Credit Bank.

question_text: When Rs 25,000 is withdrawn in cash from the company's current bank account for factory petty cash, what type of voucher is posted?
option_a: Contra Entry (Debit Petty Cash Account | Credit Bank Current Account)
option_b: Sales Entry
explanation: Transfers between internal cash and bank accounts are recorded as Contra Vouchers.

question_text: Under a fixed Petty Cash Imprest system of Rs 20,000, if factory expense vouchers total Rs 16,500 during the month, how much reimbursement is issued?
option_a: Exactly Rs 16,500 to restore the float back to Rs 20,000
explanation: The imprest system reimburses the exact total of verified expense vouchers to maintain the fixed float balance.

question_text: If a customer deposits Rs 75,000 directly into the company bank account without prior advice, how is this detected?
option_a: During daily bank statement download and BRS reconciliation
option_b: When the customer files their annual income tax return
option_d: By checking physical raw material stock
explanation: Daily bank statement verification and BRS identify unrecorded direct credits from customers.

question_text: How is a Bank Overdraft (credit balance in bank current account) presented on the balance sheet?
option_a: As a Current Liability under Short-Term Borrowings
option_b: As a Fixed Asset
explanation: A bank overdraft represents a short-term bank credit facility classified as a Current Liability on the balance sheet.

question_text: What is the primary internal financial control purpose of requiring Dual Signatures on bank payments exceeding Rs 1,00,000?
option_a: To ensure Maker-Checker authorization and prevent unauthorized cash misappropriation
option_b: To delay payments to suppliers
option_d: It is a requirement only for foreign banks
explanation: Dual signature authorization prevents fraudulent disbursements and ensures proper managerial oversight.

question_text: In commercial trade, what is a Letter of Credit (LC) issued by a buyer's bank?
option_a: A bank's formal financial guarantee that payment will be made to the seller upon presentation of compliant dispatch shipping documents
option_b: A loan taken by employees
explanation: A Letter of Credit is a bank undertaking ensuring payment to the seller upon presentation of stipulated shipping documents.

question_text: For a supply of packaging boxes within the same state (intra-state supply), which GST components are charged on the tax invoice?
option_a: CGST + SGST in equal halves (e.g. 6% CGST + 6% SGST for 12% total)
option_b: IGST only
explanation: Intra-state supplies attract CGST and SGST equally; inter-state supplies attract IGST.

question_text: What information is reported in the statutory monthly GSTR-1 return?
option_a: Invoice-level details of all outward supplies (B2B sales, B2C sales, credit notes, exports) made during the month
option_b: Employee salary and PF deductions
explanation: GSTR-1 is the monthly/quarterly return containing invoice-level details of all outward sales supplies.

question_text: What is the primary function of the monthly GSTR-3B return?
option_a: A monthly self-declaration summary return for declaring total outward tax liability, Input Tax Credit (ITC) availed, and paying net GST
option_b: An application for import license
option_d: A document for requesting bank loans
explanation: GSTR-3B is the monthly self-assessment summary return used to offset ITC against outward tax liability and pay net GST.

question_text: Under Section 16(2)(aa) of the CGST Act, can an accountant claim Input Tax Credit (ITC) on a vendor invoice that is entered in the books but missing in auto-generated GSTR-2B?
option_a: No, ITC is strictly restricted to invoices appearing in GSTR-2B filed by suppliers
option_b: Yes, 100% ITC can be claimed immediately regardless of 2B
option_c: Yes, plus an extra 20% provisional credit
option_d: Only if the vendor is located in another state
explanation: Section 16(2)(aa) legally mandates that ITC can only be availed if the supplier has filed GSTR-1 and it appears in GSTR-2B.

question_text: If a vendor invoice for Rs 5,00,000 + GST Rs 90,000 remains unpaid on 185 days from invoice date, what action is legally mandatory in GSTR-3B?
option_a: Reverse the Rs 90,000 ITC in Table 4(B) of GSTR-3B along with 18% annual interest under Section 50
option_b: Claim double the ITC
explanation: Under Rule 37, failure to pay supplier within 180 days requires ITC reversal with interest @ 18%.

question_text: Under Section 17(5) of the CGST Act, can Input Tax Credit (ITC) be claimed on GST paid for food, beverages, and catering for office staff?
option_a: No, it is specifically blocked credit under Section 17(5)(b)
option_b: Yes, 100% ITC is always claimable
option_c: Yes, but only if the food is vegetarian
explanation: Section 17(5)(b) specifically blocks ITC on food and beverages, outdoor catering, and staff personal consumption.

question_text: What is the standard TDS deduction rate under Section 194C for payments made to an Individual / HUF transport contractor with a valid PAN?
explanation: Section 194C prescribes 1% TDS for Individual/HUF contractors and 2% for Companies/Partnerships.

question_text: What is the standard TDS deduction rate under Section 194J on professional consulting fees exceeding Rs 30,000 per year?
explanation: Section 194J requires 10% TDS on professional fees and 2% on technical services.

question_text: What is the monthly due date for depositing TDS deducted during May to the Central Government via Challan 281?
option_a: 7th of June
option_b: 30th of June
explanation: TDS deducted in any month must be deposited by the 7th of the following month (except for March, which is April 30th).

question_text: If both buyer (turnover > 10 Cr) and seller (turnover > 10 Cr) cross Rs 50 Lakhs in goods transactions, who is legally obligated to deduct/collect tax?
option_a: The buyer must deduct TDS under Section 194Q @ 0.1%; Section 206C(1H) TCS will NOT apply
option_b: The seller must collect TCS; 194Q will not apply
option_c: Both must deduct and collect simultaneously
explanation: Section 194Q(5) states that if tax is deductible by buyer under Section 194Q, Section 206C(1H) TCS shall not apply.

question_text: When the company incurs Rs 2,50,000 on a major machine overhaul that increases the productive life of machinery by 4 years, what is the accounting classification?
option_a: Capital Expenditure (debited to Plant & Machinery asset account and depreciated over the extended life)
option_b: Revenue Expenditure (expensed 100% immediately to P&L)
explanation: Expenditure that enhances future economic benefits or extends the useful life of an asset is Capital Expenditure.

question_text: Under traditional double-entry rules of accounting, what is the fundamental rule for Real Accounts (e.g. Plant Machinery, Cash, Inventory)?
option_a: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out
option_b: Debit the receiver, Credit the giver
option_c: Debit all expenses and losses, Credit all incomes and gains
explanation: Real accounts (assets and property) follow the rule: 'Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out'.

question_text: When an overdue debtor owing Rs 15,000 is formally declared irrecoverable, what is the direct write-off entry?
option_a: Debit Bad Debts Account Rs 15,000 | Credit Customer Debtors Account Rs 15,000
option_b: Debit Customer Account | Credit Sales Revenue
option_c: Debit Bank Account | Credit Bad Debts
option_d: Debit Inventory Account | Credit Cash Account
explanation: Writing off an uncollectible receivable debits Bad Debts Expense and credits the Customer's ledger account.

question_text: Why must an accountant book an Accrued Expense provision entry for factory electricity consumed in March but billed in April?
option_a: To adhere to the Accrual Principle and match current month expenses against current month revenue
option_b: To evade income tax legally
option_d: To avoid paying the electricity board
explanation: Accrual accounting mandates recognizing expenses in the accounting period in which they are incurred regardless of invoice date.

question_text: When an annual factory fire insurance premium of Rs 1,20,000 is paid on October 1st (for 12 months), how much is charged to the current FY ending March 31st?
option_a: Rs 60,000 (6 months expensed to P&L, 6 months carried as Prepaid Asset on Balance Sheet)
explanation: 6 months (Oct-Mar) belongs to current FY (Rs 60,000 expensed); remaining 6 months is carried forward as a Prepaid Expense asset.

question_text: When the company earns bank fixed deposit interest of Rs 35,000 in March which will only be credited by the bank in April, what entry is posted on March 31?
option_a: Debit Accrued Interest Asset Account Rs 35,000 | Credit Interest Income P&L Account Rs 35,000
option_b: Debit Bank Account | Credit Share Capital
option_c: Debit Sales Account | Credit Interest Income
option_d: No entry until the cash is credited
explanation: Interest earned but not yet received is recorded as Accrued Income (Current Asset) on the balance sheet date.

question_text: In a double-entry Trial Balance, if total Debits equal total Credits, does it guarantee that there are zero accounting errors in the books?
option_a: No, errors of omission, errors of principle, or compensating errors may still exist
option_b: Yes, it guarantees 100% mathematical and conceptual perfection
explanation: A balanced trial balance only proves arithmetical equality of debits and credits; errors of principle or omission can still exist.

question_text: In standard corporate accounting structure, which financial statements are generated from Balance Sheet ledgers versus P&L ledgers?
option_a: Assets, Liabilities, and Equity form the Balance Sheet; Revenues, Cost of Sales, and Operating Expenses form the Profit & Loss Statement
option_b: All ledgers go to Balance Sheet only
option_c: All ledgers go to P&L only
explanation: Real and Personal accounts form the Balance Sheet (financial position), while Nominal accounts form the Profit & Loss statement.

question_text: A machine costing Rs 10,00,000 has an estimated useful life of 10 years and residual scrap value of Rs 1,00,000. Under Straight Line Method (SLM), what is the annual depreciation?
option_b: Rs 1,00,000 per year
explanation: Annual SLM Depreciation = (Cost - Scrap Value) / Useful Life = (10,00,000 - 1,00,000) / 10 = Rs 90,000.

question_text: In a Cash Flow Statement, how does an increase in Trade Receivables (Debtors) during the year affect Operating Cash Flow?
option_a: Deducted from net profit in operating activities (cash tied up in uncollected sales)
option_b: Added to net profit as cash inflow
explanation: An increase in working capital debtors indicates revenue recognized but not yet collected in cash, requiring a deduction from net profit.
